nodes.title: Maintenance window
nodes.subtitle: planned work
details: Silences alerts for the services it lists.
Always has an end time: nothing stays silenced forever.

nodes.title: Deploy freeze
nodes.subtitle: stops every pipeline
details: Set by the commander, by a SEV1, or by a rollback while it runs.
Lifted by hand once the incident is resolved.

nodes.title: Manual page
nodes.subtitle: anyone can page on-call
details: A button in the chat tool and on the status dashboard.
Opens an incident with the reporter as first contact.

nodes.title: Severity selector
nodes.subtitle: SEV1 · SEV2 · SEV3
details: SEV1: customers cannot use the product. SEV2: a feature is degraded. SEV3: no customer impact yet.
A severity chosen by hand always wins over the computed one.

nodes.title: Acknowledge
nodes.subtitle: on-call takes the incident
details: Stops the escalation timer.
The responder is incident commander until they hand over.

nodes.title: Runbook buttons
nodes.subtitle: scripted fixes
details: Restart a service, fail over a database, roll back, add capacity.
Every run is written to the incident timeline.

nodes.title: Logs
nodes.subtitle: structured, one line per request
details: Error lines are counted by fingerprint.
Kept for 14 days.

nodes.title: Metrics
nodes.subtitle: latency, errors, saturation
details: Scraped every 15 seconds from every service.
The four golden signals, per endpoint.

nodes.title: Synthetic probes
nodes.subtitle: checks from three regions
details: Log in, search and check out, every minute.
A probe failing from two regions counts; one region alone may be the network.

nodes.title: Customer reports
nodes.subtitle: tickets and the status page
details: Tickets tagged “outage” are counted per hour.
Status page subscribers can report a problem.

nodes.title: Deploy events
nodes.subtitle: what changed, and when
details: Every rollout publishes service, version and author.
Feature flag flips are published too.

nodes.title: Deduplication
nodes.subtitle: one incident, not fifty alerts
details: Alerts with the same service and symptom join the open incident.
A new symptom opens a new incident.

nodes.title: Anomaly detection
nodes.subtitle: unusual for this hour
details: Compares each metric with the same hour a week earlier.
Never pages on its own: it only adds a hint.

nodes.title: SLO burn rate
nodes.subtitle: error budget spent too fast
details: Fast burn: 2 % of the monthly budget in one hour.
Slow burn: 10 % in six hours.

nodes.title: Customer impact
nodes.subtitle: who is affected
details: Probes, tickets and errors per region and per plan.
Decides whether the status page has to speak.

nodes.title: Change correlation
nodes.subtitle: did a deploy cause it?
details: Links an alert to deploys of the same service in the previous 30 minutes.
Shown on the incident as the likely cause.

nodes.title: Escalation policy
nodes.subtitle: who is woken up
details: Primary on-call first; secondary after 10 minutes without an acknowledgement.
A SEV1 also pages the engineering manager at once.

nodes.title: Triage
nodes.subtitle: open, merge or drop
details: Opens an incident for a manual page, a fast burn or an outage tag.
Merges duplicates; drops alerts inside a maintenance window.

nodes.title: Resolution
nodes.subtitle: when it is over
details: Resolved when the signals stay healthy for 15 minutes.
Reopens if the same symptom returns within an hour.

nodes.title: Severity
nodes.subtitle: how bad it is
details: Starts from customer impact.
The commander can override it with the severity selector.

nodes.title: Communication plan
nodes.subtitle: what to say, and to whom
details: SEV1 and SEV2 update the status page every 30 minutes.
Internal updates go to the incident channel.

nodes.title: Rollback advisor
nodes.subtitle: undo the last change?
details: Suggests a rollback when the change correlation is strong.
Never suggests one during a database migration.

nodes.title: Auto-remediation
nodes.subtitle: known problem, known fix
details: Runs a runbook when a symptom matches one exactly.
Gives up after two attempts and pages a human.

nodes.title: Post-incident review
nodes.subtitle: learning, not blame
details: Required for SEV1 and SEV2.
Collects the timeline, the decisions and the follow-up tasks.

nodes.title: Pager
nodes.subtitle: phone, SMS and push
details: Repeats every 2 minutes until someone acknowledges.
Ignores do-not-disturb for a SEV1.

nodes.title: Incident channel
nodes.subtitle: one per incident
details: Created with the timeline, the likely cause and the runbooks.
Archived after the review.

nodes.title: Status page
nodes.subtitle: public updates
details: Drafted from the customer impact; a person publishes it.
Subscribers get each update by email.

nodes.title: Rollback
nodes.subtitle: previous version, every region
details: Blue-green: traffic moves back in under a minute.
Sets the deploy freeze while it runs.

nodes.title: Scaling
nodes.subtitle: more capacity
details: Adds instances when saturation is the symptom.
Capped, so a loop cannot spend without limit.

nodes.title: Follow-up tickets
nodes.subtitle: tasks from the review
details: Every action item gets an owner and a due date.
Open items are listed in the weekly report.

nodes.title: Time-series store
nodes.subtitle: metrics and events
details: 13 months of history, downsampled after 30 days.
Backs every graph on the incident channel.

nodes.title: On-call schedule
nodes.subtitle: rotations and overrides
details: Weekly rotations with a primary and a secondary.
Overrides for holidays and swaps.

nodes.title: Configuration repository
nodes.subtitle: alerts and policies as code
details: Alert rules, escalation policies and runbooks are reviewed like any code change.
Merged changes apply within a minute.

nodes.title: Audit log
nodes.subtitle: who did what
details: Every acknowledgement, override, runbook run and rollback.
Append-only and kept for a year.

nodes.title: Event bus
nodes.subtitle: every signal passes through it
details: Signals, alerts and actions are events with a schema.
Consumers can replay the last 7 days.
